items.title: Account blocking by LinkedIn to be challenged through civil suit, not writ petition: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has held that a writ petition is not maintainable against LinkedIn or its resident grievance officer over their decision to block/restrict an account [Mayank Jain v. Union of India & Ors] . Its operations remain private in nature, and no governmental mandate delegates any traditional State function to it. Hardeep Singh Puri, now India’s Petroleum Minister, sitting across a table from Jeffrey Epstein, the convicted sex offender who counted some of the world’s most powerful people among his associates. items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Monday inaugurated the Jharkhand High Court’s data centre. Speaking at the event, he stressed the need to protect sensitive judicial records against unauthorised access, loss and disruption. “Judicial records contain sensitive information and must be protected against unauthorised access, loss and disruption. Cybersecurity, reliable backup arrangements, regular testing and trained technical personnel are essential to maintaining public confidence in digital systems,” he stated. The data centre project represents an investment of approximately ₹25 crore. Its value, the CJI noted, would be measured by improvements in court functioning and the experience of litigants, rather than the equipment installed. items.summary: The Rajasthan High Court full bench on Monday held that writ petitions arising from criminal matters must be registered separately as criminal writ petitions [Ravi Kumar v State Of Rajasthan & Ors.] . A Bench of Chief Justice Sanjay K Agrawal , Justice Sameer Jain and Justice Anuroop Singhi overruled an earlier verdict rendered in this regard by a division bench headed by former acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma. The full bench observed that the July 2026 division bench ruling of the Court had failed to consider Rule 315(1)(h) of the Rajasthan High Court Rules, which requires writ petitions arising from criminal matters to be registered separately. "The aforesaid decision in Jiya failed to consider or give effect to the statutory mandate embodied in Rule 315(1)(h) of the Rajasthan High Court Rules, its ratio, insofar as it prohibits criminal-side registration of such writ applications, is held to be per incuriam, having been rendered in ignorance of, or without due consideration of, a relevant statutory provision," held the full bench. items.title: Kerala: 17-year-old boy murdered after being used as bait to lure another teen
items.summary: The 17-year-old boy murdered in Thiruvananthapuram was allegedly used as bait to lure another teenager whom the accused had planned to kill over a personal dispute, the city police have said. Investigators suspect that the murder was part of a premeditated plan, with the first accused – a 17-year-old boy – discussing the killing days in advance and sharing a photograph of an axe with an 18-year-old girl who is among those arrested. City Police Commissioner Arul RB Krishna said the accused had intended to use the victim, MD Abhiram, to bring his friend to an isolated location in Pangappara. However, when Abhiram did not cooperate, the plan allegedly took a different turn, resulting in his murder. Abhiram, a plus-two student and resident of Sreekaryam, went missing on the night of November 1. His body was found in an isolated area at Pangappara, near Sreekaryam, on the evening of November 2. The police subsequently arrested three persons, a 17-year-old boy (first accused), an 18-year-old girl (third accused) and Umar Muqthar (second accused), who had been detained under the Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act (KAAPA).
